message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: .NET

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main", "rc" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main", "rc" ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
    - name: Setup .NET
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6.0.0
      with:
        dotnet-version: 10.0.x
    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/packages.lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-
    - name: Build
      run: |
        if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
          VERSION_SUFFIX="rc.${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}.${{ github.run_number }}"
        else
          VERSION_SUFFIX=""
        fi
        dotnet build -p:VersionSuffix="${VERSION_SUFFIX}" -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs dotnet build on every push/PR and restores NuGet packages each time. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency_cache pattern is supported by measured CI workflow evidence (actions/cache@v4 added before dependency installation) showing reduced elapsed time. Preconditions hold: repeated dependency fetching is measurable from the CI history, and cache inputs can be keyed to lockfiles/environment. No equivalent cache exists. Adding a NuGet package cache before the build step preserves the build command, required checks, and coverage; it adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing, deployment, or new network access beyond the already-evidenced actions/cache usage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}

- Repeated dependency fetching is measurable ✓ (CI history shows repeated runs)
- Cache inputs include lockfile and environment ✓ (.NET has lockfiles)

- Mutable or untrusted cached content - NuGet packages are trusted
- An equivalent cache already exists - no cache exists in the workflow
